name: Qwen4-Max
archDisplay: Sparse MoE on the new Qwen4 architecture: 2.4T backbone parameters, 71B activated per token, plus 328B N-gram Embedding parameters; Gated DeltaNet + Qwen Sparse Attention, gated residuals; 1M-token context, native text/image/video input
note: Alibaba's first Qwen4 model, announced Nov 16, 2026 (Qwen blog; Vals lists Nov 15, likely a time-zone difference) after a Token-Plan-only preview from Nov 11. API only: weights are private (Vals) and the post makes no open-weight commitment for Max. It is the first model in the Qwen4 family; the post compares it with Qwen3.8-Max throughout, but predecessors must share a family, so predecessor is null. Price is the Singapore (international) pay-as-you-go list, one tier up to 1M tokens, thinking or not ($0.075 cache read; $1.413/$4.24 in other regions). Thinking is on by default with low/high/xhigh effort. Context limits per Alibaba Cloud docs: 991,808 input (non-thinking), 131,072 output (non-thinking), 262,144 thinking plus answer. Vals AI's independent run adds Terminal-Bench 4.0 48.48 (#15 of 65; Qwen3.8-Max-0902 scored 38.89). NOT FILED: the launch post's benchmark chart is an image, so its figures (DeepSWE v1.1, Terminal-Bench 4.0, HLE, APEX-Agents v1.1, JobBench and others, as transcribed by third parties) are not filed; the text-stated Work360 52.69 and Last Secure Code Bench 31.8% have no corpus column; Vals Index 63.20, Finance Agent v2.1 66.68, EMB v1.1 70.83, HLAB-Vals-1.1 21.25, Legal Research Bench 41.35, Tax Agent Bench 40.35 and Vibe Code Bench v1.1 86.66 have no corpus column. No Text Arena row yet.

results.notes: Terminal-Bench 4.0, Vals AI independent run (mini-swe-agent harness, avg@3; ±0.88) via Alibaba as provider, xhigh reasoning effort; #15 of 65 per the Vals model page (its update text says 48.49). No fallbacks shown.
